method_as_stated: MOLECULAR DYNAMICS: Langevin dynamics in HOOMD-blue v2.9.7. Each particle is five spheres, four lobes and one central sphere standing for the four patches; the pair potential combines an Alexander-de Gennes brush repulsion with Asakura-Oosawa depletion (details in the SI). PHASE DIAGRAM BY MELTING: for each compression and size ratio, 600 particles are started in cubic diamond and run 1e8 steps at time step 0.0001; stability is the fraction still diamond by common-neighbour analysis in OVITO. Starting from a disordered gas was tried and found spontaneous diamond only for some parameter sets, nucleation not being seen within reachable times over much of the space. UMBRELLA SAMPLING: one pair with the same potential plus a harmonic restraint on the centre separation, spring constant 3,333 kT/um^2, 40 windows with rest lengths from 1.16 um to 3 um, 2e8 steps each with the second half used for WHAM; parameters matched to experiment (compression 0.6, size ratio 1.21, depletant-to-lobe radius ratio 0.02). MONTE CARLO INTEGRATION of the excluded-volume overlap for a pair fixed in the staggered, patch-facing conformation, depletant radius 0.02 of the lobe radius for the experimental case and 0.01 to 0.20 at compression 0.7 for the comparison with pairwise additivity. EXPERIMENT: four polystyrene lobes (about 1 um) on a TPM patch core, compressed in about 20 vol% THF; depletants Pluronic F127 micelles (cmc about 0.1% w/v, hydrodynamic radius about 10 nm), 12-nm silica (Ludox HS-40), titania and PEO; assembly at room temperature in 500 mM NaCl (Debye length 0.43 nm) in 100 um x 2 mm x 5 cm HMDS-treated capillaries; index-matched PPFPMA particles imaged in z steps of 200 nm; fixing by palindromic DNA and 310-nm UV thymine photodimerisation.

note: Sequel to He et al. 2020 (src_he_2020_colloidal_diamond). The two papers disagree about WHERE diamond forms relative to the kissing geometry, and that is not a conflict: DNA patch-patch binding and depletion are different interactions, and this paper says so.
